direction.name: Colour chapters
direction.idea: Every section is a chapter with its own flat colour, floor to ceiling. The page reads like a set of posters hung in a row, held together by one typeface and one grid. The colours are not decoration: they come from the subject (the brand's packaging, the artist's record sleeves, the product's own colour ways, the categories of the content) and each chapter's colour means that chapter. Decide the sequence like a designer orders a book: a strong opener, a quiet second, a surprise in the middle, a dark or very light closer.
direction.composition: Sections are full-bleed fields, each at least 90svh tall, butted directly against each other with no gap and no divider. Inside every field the same 12-column grid and the same margins apply, and each field holds one thing: a huge heading (8–12vw) with a small paragraph, or one photograph with a caption, or one list. Text colour is chosen per field for strong contrast (ink or paper, never grey). Headings start on the same left edge in every chapter, so the eye feels the system as colours change. The navigation and the footer take the colours of the first and last chapter.
direction.typography: One typeface in two weights. Headings very large and tight; body 18–20px. Because colour is loud, the type stays plain: no italics, no second face.
direction.colour: Four to six flat fields used at full strength, one per section, each with its assigned text colour. No tints, no gradients between them: the hard edge where two fields meet is the look.
direction.imagery: Sparing. One photograph or object per chapter at most, either cut out and sitting directly on the colour, or a plain rectangle with generous colour around it. Photographs should be simple enough not to fight the field.
direction.richness: Colour at scale. A whole screen of one saturated colour is rich on its own, so a chapter needs few elements; it still needs its content at full size, because a coloured screen with one small line on it reads as empty.
direction.pitfalls: Check contrast on every field with the palette's assigned ink. Do not put cards on the fields. Do not use more than six colours. Two neighbouring fields should differ clearly in lightness as well as hue.

hero.name: Mosaic masthead, title on axis
hero.blueprint: The top 52% of the viewport is a full-width masthead band built as a gutterless mosaic: a CSS grid of 6 columns and 2 rows in which four cells are photographs (object-fit: cover, all greyscale via filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.05)) and the rest are flat tiles in two or three palette colours. One photograph spans two columns and one colour tile spans both rows; cells butt together with no gap. The header lies flush on the band's upper edge: the wordmark in a solid ink block at far left, a flat accent-coloured tab holding three text links that runs from the block to 42% of the width, and the single action as a text link at the far right. Below the band, on the paper ground: a standfirst of one sentence at 20px on the 16px left margin, max 30ch, and, starting exactly at 42% of the width, the title on two lines at clamp(64px, 8.3vw, 128px), medium weight, tracking -0.06em, leading 0.9, running to the right margin. The title's first baseline sits about 110px under the band.
hero.mobile: The band becomes a mosaic of 3 columns and 2 rows taking the top 38% of the screen: two photographs and four colour tiles. The header is a single row above it with the wordmark block and a menu word. The axis collapses to the 16px left margin: the title at 13vw on two lines, then the standfirst at 17px beneath it. The action sits as a text link at the foot of the screen.
hero.headline: The title of the report, programme or product, 2-5 words, at most 26 characters across two lines.

type.note: One neo-grotesk doing everything: semibold headings pulled tight, small regular text, no capitals and no second voice. Suits software, hardware and studio pages that want to look exact and unshowy.

motion.name: Masked headline
motion.description: On load, each line of the headline rises from behind its own baseline, about 900ms with a strong ease-out, the second line 110ms after the first; the supporting sentence and the action then fade up together. Nothing else on the page performs. Because headlines are two lines at most, you author the line breaks and wrap each line yourself. Recipe: 'Masked line reveal' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Edge-to-edge heavy paragraph
sections.blueprint: A full-bleed flat colour field, at least 90svh tall, filled by one paragraph and nothing else. The paragraph is 35–55 words in the heaviest weight at clamp(36px, 5vw, 76px), leading 0.98, left-aligned, running from a 16px left margin to a 16px right margin so its lines reach both edges; use `text-wrap: pretty` and no hyphenation. No heading: the paragraph is the section. In two or three places a word-sized gap (an inline-block spacer 2.5em wide) opens inside a line. One small photograph, 9vw wide at 4:5 with square corners, is absolutely placed over the first two lines, rotated 4 degrees, covering parts of two words; a second chip at 6vw may sit in one of the gaps. Text takes the field's assigned ink at full contrast. The field butts against the section above with no space between them. On a page without images, drop the chips and close the gaps.
sections.mobile: The same field and weight at 9.5vw with leading 1.0 and 14px margins, so each line holds two or three words and the paragraph runs about fourteen lines. Remove the inline gaps. The photograph chip grows to 26vw and sits over the right end of lines three and four, still tilted.

sections.name: Square plate, spare text
sections.blueprint: One flat field split 50/50, at least 88svh tall. Left half: a single square photograph filling the half's width minus 40px margins, vertically centred, square corners. A large simple shape may be laid over it to turn the photograph into the object it stands for: a ring 86% of its width with a 6px stroke and a small solid dot at the centre makes a record; a notch cut by clip-path makes a ticket stub. Right half, a flex column with space-between: at the top a row of three plain text tabs at 18px (editions, years, variants), the active one in full ink and the others at 40%; in the middle the title, two to four words at 32–40px bold, with a 34ch description 48px below; along the bottom two filled rectangular cells side by side, each half the column wide and 72px tall, acting as the two actions, one in ink and one a tone off the field.
sections.mobile: The square photograph comes first at full width with 16px margins. The tabs sit under it as one row at 17px. Then the title at 28px, the description, and the two action cells stacked, each full width and 60px tall.

sections.name: Mosaic of unlike tiles
sections.blueprint: A 12-column grid with 8px gaps and rows of 96px, filled with no empty cells and no outlines. Six to eight filled tiles in four sizes only: 6×5, 6×3, 3×3 and 3×2 (columns × rows). The rule that keeps it from being a card grid: no two neighbouring tiles hold the same kind of thing. One tile is the heading alone, two to four words at 4vw, top-left. One is a photograph covering its tile. One is a single figure at 6vw with a caption. One is a short list of four lines at 20px. The others are a single sentence each at 28–32px. Text sits top-left with 24px padding; tiles holding one sentence leave their lower half empty. Tile fills: the ground one tone darker, two palette colours, and photographs. One corner radius everywhere, either 0 or 8px.
sections.mobile: Two columns with 6px gaps. The heading tile and the photograph tile span both columns; sentence tiles span both at their natural height; the figure and list tiles sit side by side as a pair of squares. Order: heading, photograph, pair, sentence, sentence.

sections.name: Two columns, highlighted words
sections.blueprint: The story is set as text far larger than anything else on the page: 110–160 words at clamp(22px, 2.1vw, 32px), tight leading 1.18, in the soft ink, flowing through two columns that fill the full width between 24px margins (`columns: 2; column-gap: 32px`, justified, with hyphenation on). No heading. The name at the start is in full ink. Six or seven single words or short phrases carry a flat highlighter background in three or four palette colours, built with an inline `background-color`, `box-decoration-break: clone` and 0.1em of horizontal padding; they mark the facts a scanning reader wants (a place, a year, a client, a skill). The final short sentence is highlighted entire in the strongest colour and is the link to contact. Padding 120px top and bottom. No image and no portrait.
sections.mobile: One column at 20px, left-aligned and unjustified, leading 1.25, with 18px margins. Keep four or five highlights so no line carries two. The final highlighted sentence sits on its own line with 24px above it and works as a full-width tap target.

sections.name: The action tile
sections.blueprint: The close is one row of the board. Three filled tiles sit side by side with 8–14px gaps, all 360px tall and sharing one radius: a wide centre tile spanning columns 3–10 in the accent colour, flanked by two narrow tiles (columns 1–2 and 11–12) that run off the left and right viewport edges, as if the row had been cropped from a longer one. The centre tile holds, left-aligned and vertically centred with 40px padding: a heading of three to five words at 40px, two lines at 17px, and the action. The action is either one rectangular button or an email field 420px wide in the paper colour with the submit button nested inside its right end. The flanking tiles hold no text: one is a photograph covering the tile, the other a flat palette colour. No shadows, no outlines.
sections.mobile: The accent tile runs full width, about 300px tall, heading at 28px, field and button stacked at full width. The two flanking tiles follow beneath as a pair, each half width and 120px tall, with the same gap and the same radius.

sections.name: Name first, places under it
sections.blueprint: The wordmark opens the footer instead of closing it. On a full-bleed field in the page's inverse or final chapter colour, the name spans the full content width as the first thing, its cap line pushed 8% above the footer's top edge so the tops of the letters are sliced off by the section (`overflow: hidden` and a negative top margin in `em`). 72px beneath, a two-part row: columns 1–5 list the places or ways to reach the studio (cities, or email and telephone), one per line at 32–36px in the accent ink, each a link; columns 7–12 hold three columns of small links at 15px, top-aligned with the first place. A final row 96px lower carries the legal line at the left and a back-to-top text link at the right, both 13px. The field is about 90svh tall, and nothing sits between the wordmark and the row but space.
sections.mobile: The sliced wordmark stays at the top, fitted to the width. Places follow as a list at 26px, then the link columns two across at 15px. Legal line and back-to-top link share the last row at 12px, at opposite margins.

references.name: Anidachi
references.idea: A toy brand built from one custom modular wordmark and one 3D device, both of which change colour with each full-bleed candy-coloured section.
references.hero: A saturated sky-blue field covering the top 92% of the viewport. The custom modular wordmark is repeated in four stacked rows, each spanning the full width inside 30px margins, drawn tone-on-tone in a slightly lighter blue that brightens row by row toward the bottom, so the name works as wallpaper. A tiny white pixel-cat mark sits top-left; a white rounded button with blue text top-right. A 3D flower-shaped toy device hangs on a carabiner from the top edge at centre, barely entered on desktop and fully visible on mobile, where it covers the pattern. A pale ice section starts at the bottom edge.
references.type: AnidachiDisplay is custom modular lettering: monoline rounded strokes on a square grid, unicase forms, used at 7-10vw. Body and UI in Ease, a soft rounded geometric sans, at 20px. Text is always coloured to its section, never black.
references.colour: #24c0fe #eff9fb #b6c814 #ff6b2b #ffffff #000000 — Each section is one flat saturated field (sky blue, ice, chartreuse, orange) with type in a single contrasting tint of the same family or white. The 3D device is recoloured to match its section.
references.imagery: A glossy flower-shaped handheld with cream buttons and a small black screen showing pixel-art animal characters, hung from a metal clasp. Pixel sprites also appear loose on the page and as a giant low-contrast watermark.
references.layout: Full-bleed colour sections of one to two screens with 30px margins. Each holds one giant display phrase at an edge, one small text block, and the 3D device crossing section boundaries. Alignment shifts section to section: centred, left column, bottom-left.

sections.description: Pale ice section. Centred: the small mascot mark and wordmark in sky blue at about 9vw, followed by a two-line statement in the rounded sans at 7vw in the same blue. Below, a left column 370px wide holds a three-line 24px lead and small paragraphs, all blue on ice; a pixel-art cat sprite stands in the right half, and a pill-outlined email field with a round arrow button ends the block.

Chartreuse full-bleed section. A title in the modular display face runs edge to edge in white at about 10vw across the top. The 3D device, recoloured olive to match, hangs from its clasp at left-centre and overlaps a diagonal ribbon of translucent rounded-square tiles, each holding a tinted character, running from lower-left to upper-right and off the edge.

Solid orange section, almost empty. A three-line 14px white paragraph sits near the top, right of centre; the bottom-left holds a two-line hyphenated phrase in the display face at roughly 9vw, white, hugging the left margin and the bottom edge. The lower edge of the device intrudes from the section above.

Ice ground with an enormous pixel-art face in a barely darker green tint as a watermark filling the frame. Lime wordmark lower-left at about 300px wide, three stacked lime links at centre, one link at right, tiny copyright beneath the logo.

steal: Repeat the wordmark as tone-on-tone rows filling the hero, stepping the tint row by row, so the brand name is the background pattern.
Give every section one saturated colour, set all its text in a single contrasting tint, and recolour the 3D product to match.
Anchor a giant two-line display phrase to the bottom-left corner of an otherwise empty colour field, with one small paragraph far away at the top.

references.name: Warm & Fuzzy
references.idea: A showreel-first studio site in which every section takes one flat, loud colour (blue, black, yellow) under heavy grotesk type and a chunky custom wordmark.
references.hero: The showreel plays full-bleed with a visible film-grain overlay and no scrim. A chunky hand-cut wordmark sits top left, 16px from the edges; the same top line continues with a one-sentence status link, a tiny thumbnail beside the latest project's name, and three caps links at the far right, all white over the footage. A small green caps play label floats at dead centre. The tagline is anchored bottom left, 16px from both edges, in white grotesk caps at 47px (3.3vw) on one line spanning 56% of the width. A tiny square pause control sits bottom right.
references.type: SuisseIntl throughout, rendering heavy, tracked -0.027em: a 47px caps tagline, a caps section title at 9.4vw, statement paragraphs around 5vw with tight leading, and 10 to 11px caps captions. The logo is custom chunky lettering with wobbly cut-paper counters.
references.colour: #000000 #190bb6 #f7dd47 #ffffff #e9479f #1fc27a — Each section is a flat field: ultramarine blue, black, yellow, then blue again. White type on blue and black, black on yellow; a green play label is the only small accent.
references.imagery: Commercial stills and video (candy-coloured CG worlds, product renders, live-action frames) in square-cornered thumbnails of mixed aspect ratios, with a grain layer over the whole page and floating glossy 3D sticker objects.
references.layout: Tight 16px outer margins and edge-to-edge type. Sections are told apart by background colour rather than spacing: a blue statement set in the right two-thirds, a black packed work wall, a yellow full-width paragraph, a blue footer.

sections.description: On black, a tiny caps motto sits top left, then a caps section title at about 9vw flush left with a small underlined link at the far right on its baseline. Beneath, thumbnails pack into an uneven wall: widths vary from one-sixth to one-half of the page, heights differ, gaps are about 8px and rows do not align. Under each image a 10px caps line gives the project name left and the year in grey right.

A yellow field filled edge to edge by one paragraph in black heavy grotesk at roughly 5vw with very tight leading, left-aligned at the 16px margin. Several lines contain deliberate word-sized gaps, as if the text flowed around something, and a small tilted image chip floats over the first lines, covering parts of words.

A full-screen blue field. A top row of tiny caps, email left and three links right, sits above a hairline. A glossy 3D sticker object hangs near the top centre. The chunky wordmark runs the full page width at the bottom in white, about a fifth of the viewport tall, above a bar of tiny caps links divided by vertical hairlines.

steal: Give every section one flat saturated background and change it at each section break, keeping type strictly black or white.
Pack work thumbnails at mixed widths and heights with 8px gaps and a two-part micro caption (name left, year right) under each.
End with the wordmark at full page width on a colour field, with all utility links reduced to a tiny caps bar split by vertical hairlines.
